Covers the introduction and every section 13.1-13.11 in order; the few numericals (bond-energy and E° differences, oxidation states, simple mole/mass ratios from the chapter's balanced equations, with any extra atomic mass stated in the question) were recomputed in Python; none repeats the chapter exercise. Book corrections followed: chlorine is a gas at room temperature, F₂ + 2X⁻ → 2F⁻ + X₂, X⁻ + Ag⁺ → AgX, 2HBr(g) + H₂SO₄ → Br₂ + SO₂ + 2H₂O, HI is a gas, Cl reduced from 0 to -1, hot NaOH gives 5NaCl + NaClO₃. The conflicting fluorine colour of 13.2 is not used.
Every question carries a book_ref (topic id and exact words of that topic's English lesson), verified by tools.py.
The Roman Urdu file has the same checkpoints, order and book_refs; each prompt keeps the English question with the Roman Urdu meaning in brackets.
